title: Siphon cohort quiet-deploy scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick, low-risk handoff for a small client-facing change that needs production verification with minimal noise. This is a personal scratchpad — not the canonical runbook. Use for sequencing and ad-hoc notes.

High-level approach:
- Siphon ~0.5% of total traffic into ephemeral cohorts (by hashed client_id % 200 == X). Keep cohorts small and short-lived.
- Use feature-flag + model-pin combo: route cohort to new binary (v2-handler) + model variant (quantized v1.3) to validate latency and output drift simultaneously.
- Do not increase cohort size until both latency and quality checks are green for 60m.

Cohort design notes:
- Cohort key: hashed(client_id + region) -> stable across retries but opaque.
- Cohort size plan: 0.25% (30 min) -> 0.5% (60 min) -> 1% (2h) -> hold. Stop on any threshold breach.
- Sticky sessions: enable sticky routing on cohort cookies for the session life (24h). Avoid split sessions mid-conversation.

Warmup strategy:
- Pre-warm GPUs with synthetic short-context requests (seed prompts) to populate KV cache. Do 2 rounds spaced 5m apart.
- For clients with long context usage, run 10 sample long-context primes during warmup to catch kernel slow paths.
- Ensure LRU prefetch is disabled for this run (we want pure behavior).

Metrics to watch (immediate):
- Error rate (5xx + internal errors): abort if > 0.8% sustained for 2 consecutive 5m windows.
- Latency p90/p95: abort if p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.6 or absolute p95 > 1.2s for text-gen endpoints.
- Token generation step-failures (OOM, kernel-fail): immediate abort and pinback.
- Output quality quick checks: sampling of diffs on typical prompts (see "quick-eval checklist" below).
- Cost delta: watch per-token compute cost; if > 30% increase sustained, escalate to infra.

Telemetry queries (examples to run from Console):
- error-rate: SELECT count(*) filter(status >= 500) / count(*) FROM requests WHERE route = 'chat.generate' AND timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes';
- latency-trend: SELECT percentile(p90, 0.95), percentile(p95, 0.99) FROM request_latency WHERE cohort = 'siphon-001' AND timestamp > now() - interval '15 minutes';
- kv-cache-hit: SELECT avg(kv_cache_hit) FROM requests WHERE cohort = 'siphon-001' AND timestamp > now() - interval '30 minutes';

Quick-eval checklist (manual sampling):
- Pick 10 queries from production log (variety: short prompt, long prompt, multi-turn).
- Compare outputs from baseline vs cohort v2 for hallucination/formatting drift. Flag if > 2 of 10 show meaningful regression.
- Run automated BLEU/ROUGE-like heuristics for structured outputs (if available).

Rollback and pinback steps (fast path):
- Feature-flag kill: flip FF "siphon-sandbox" -> off. (Primary mitigation).
- Model pin: ensure route fallback to pinned-stable (model: rwd-stable-v1) using routing policy priority.
- Instance kill: if FF flip not effective (rare), scale down new handler pool via autoscaler to 0 and scale baseline back up.
- Post-rollback: run quick smoke tests, mark incident draft, notify on-call.

Commands & ops snippets (for quick copy):
- Flip FF via admin: curl -X POST https://console/api/flags/siphon-sandbox -d '{"enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
- Scale handler pool: kubectl -n serving set replicas deploy/new-handler 0 --context=prod-eu
- Pin model route: POST https://console/api/routes/pin -d '{"route":"chat.generate","model":"rwd-stable-v1","until":"2024-12-31T23:59:00Z"}'

Communications checklist:
- Pre-deploy (30m): Slack #deploy-alert with expected cohort size/time and on-call contacts. Include quick rollback steps.
- If throttled/abort: notify #ops and customer-success, include timeline and incident ticket.
- Post 24h: short summary to #eng and #pm with major observations and recommendation (roll forward / extend / abort).

Edge cases and gotchas noted during dry-runs:
- Some clients rekey client_id each session -> cohort churn. If churn > 15% of cohort, increase session-key affinity to 'session_id' or change hashing.
- Long-tailed latency arises when batch sizes shrink unexpectedly; probe batch histograms before roll.
- Cache-prefill mismatch: avoid mixing prefilled KV from different model variants. If mixing unavoidable, fully restart instance pool between baseline and cohort.

Open ACTION items (personal):
- [ ] Ask infra to reserve two warm nodes in us-west for 45m starting 2024-11-10 09:00 PT. (ticket INF-482)
- [ ] Push small PR to add cohort tag to request logs for easier filtering (GH PR linked above).
- [ ] Draft a one-paragraph customer-facing note for CS in case of visible client impact.
- [ ] Add a short watch-query to dashboard: "siphon_cohort_p95_ratio" comparing cohort vs baseline.

Notes from last mini-run (lessons):
- Warmup cadence of 3 rounds (0m, +3m, +10m) reduced first-token p95 by ~18%. Keep that.
- One client had API key rotation mid-cohort — gating on session cookie was better in practice.
- Observed transient mem spike on quantized kernel migration; mitigated by staggered instance restart. Add stagger plan to next run.

Decision anchors (for escalation):
- Non-severity escape: any sustained user-visible regression (formatting/hallucination) -> rollback.
- Severity: any client complaint or 5xx spike + p95>baseline*1.6 -> abort and postmortem.

End-of-run checklist (post hold period):
- Collect 1h/6h/24h metrics snapshots and attach to ticket.
- Run 50-sample automated quality checks and summarize.
- Decide: roll forward (increase cohort and schedule next ramp), extend (hold longer), or abort (pinback + cleanup).
- If roll forward: update FF dates and notify #deploy-alert with new plan.

Personal scribbles / heuristics:
- Quiet deploys are about minimizing blast radius; prefer time-window and cohort hashing over manual VIP-level routing.
- Metric thresholds should bias toward safety for first 48h; be conservative when unknown client patterns exist.
- When in doubt, kill FF. It is cheap.

Random TODOs for follow-up research:
- Explore ephemeral cohort buckets that auto-rebalance to maintain fixed absolute user count rather than percentage.
- Investigate automatic KV cache priming API for curated prompt sets.
- Check if the telemetry pipeline can surfaced cohort-delta alerts automatically.

End notes: keep this doc as a scratchpad. Convert to formal runbook once a couple of successful quiet deploys complete.

-- SP
